openings.claim: Thumb-actuated captive plunger may reseat the clip; its guided head is predicted to align the impulse with the clip axis and retain moving parts.
openings.discriminator: Adequate seating is predicted, with no seating-performance ordering against D2. Failure to seat, grip loss, or wiring contact defeats adequacy.
openings.probe: Proposed: exercise orientations on a wiring surrogate; assess seating, part retention, secure one-hand operation and grip.
openings.uncertainty: Thumb force and guidance tolerance remain unresolved; geometry is hypothetical and the captive-head concept is drawing-only.

openings.claim: A captive spring head held by an elastomer latch may deliver repeatable taps: stored spring energy is predicted to reduce dependence on thumb speed, contingent on compatible latch material.
openings.discriminator: Predicts lower tap-to-tap variation than D1, not higher seating success; equivalent or greater variation defeats that comparison.
openings.probe: Proposed: establish compatible latch availability before repeated surrogate strokes against D1; assess variation, seating, one-hand grip, captivity and wiring clearance.
openings.uncertainty: Indispensable material availability and release stability are unknown; feasibility gates the trial.

lineage.reason: Preserves guided axial impulse, captivity and adequacy claim.
Preserves material dependency, stored-energy relation and variation comparison.
Dropping an unattached weight uses gravity for impact but violates no-falling-parts even if seating succeeds. Energy sufficiency and wiring contact remain unknown; no overhead trial.

decision: Synthetic proposals only; confirmation names the phase, not evidence. Retain D1/D2 for gated surrogate assessment. Every option must maintain one-hand operation and retention, allow no detached part to fall, and avoid adjacent wiring; unresolved constraints prevent acceptance.
